workflowArticle.title: iCloud quota or Mac disk space? Identify the constraint before cleaning
workflowArticle.intent: Help Mac owners distinguish a cloud-storage quota problem from local storage pressure before considering an iCloud Cleaner replacement.
workflowArticle.distinctFromComparison: Problem diagnosis and decision workflow, not a repeated product matrix.
outline: Identify which storage limit is involved
Confirm sync/download state and independent backups before considering changes
Treat .git history, project dependencies and photos as different data classes
Evaluate documented tool scope without promising iCloud-plan savings
evidenceNeeded: Official Apple iCloud Drive/Photos storage and sync-deletion guidance before any procedural advice
Operational official iCloud Cleaner docs and screenshots
workflowArticle.interactionHandoff: A non-mutating checklist: which quota is full, where originals live, whether a backup exists. No disk access, upload, account login or delete buttons.
workflowArticle.visualPlan: Required cleared competitor UI directly after lead; labeled Breathing Room Space example later. Neither asset gate is waived.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs iCloud Cleaner: verify the storage job first
comparison.intent: Concise adjacent-fit comparison only after identity/availability evidence exists.
rows: Cloud quota versus Mac disk investigation
comparison.linkPolicy: Proposed routes only; do not create or imply these pages are live.

advantagesAndTradeoffs: If official sources later confirm the listing's iCloud-focused workflow, that specificity may fit cloud-quota investigation better; not verified now and no purchase recommendation is justified.
Breathing Room, which we build, has documented Mac storage and grouped-process investigation in its preview; this does not establish iCloud-plan migration equivalence.

Breathing Room register caveats: identified release 0.1.0-preview.1, macOS 13+, universal installer advertised but physical Intel untested; Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed/notarized; Python 3.10+ prerequisite.

Free local desktop capabilities are separate from optional AI Care advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year, renewing with applicable tax. Hosted AI needs authentication/internet and can receive paths/process/storage data; not entirely offline.

Daily care needs app running and exact saved approvals; optional automatic verified Ruff-cache mode prevents an unconditional never-deletes-without-asking claim. No native execution or savings comparison tested here.
